name: Sodium thiosulfate
typicalUses: Quenching excess halogens or oxidants in workups
chemoselectivity: Reduces I₂ cleanly to I⁻ (1 mol I₂ per 2 mol S₂O₃²⁻)
pitfalls: Disproportionates in acid to S (cloudy precipitate) and SO₂

name: Iron(II) sulfate
chemoselectivity: Fe²⁺ is a mild reductant: oxidised to Fe³⁺
pitfalls: Solutions slowly oxidise in air, so standardise them shortly before use

name: Zinc metal
typicalUses: With acid: H₂ and reduction of nitro groups
chemoselectivity: More reducing than H₂ (E° < 0), so it dissolves in dilute non-oxidising acids
pitfalls: Amphoteric: it also dissolves in strong alkali as zincate, releasing H₂

name: Sodium metal
typicalUses: Drying ethers and hydrocarbons (with benzophenone as indicator)
chemoselectivity: Reacts with water and alcohols to give H₂ and hydroxide/alkoxide
pitfalls: Never use to dry halogenated solvents (explosive reaction)
